title: Everyone Thinks Jiuzhaigou's Lakes Are Photoshopped. They're Not | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone thinks Jiuzhaigou's turquoise lakes are Photoshopped. They aren't — the water really is that blue.

The whole valley sits on carbonate limestone. Glacial meltwater dissolves it and redeposits pale travertine along the lakebed; add extremely pure water, algae and sunlight through the shallows, and you get those unreal blues and greens — no filter. There are over 100 lakes, several so clear you can count the sunken logs on the bottom. Peak-season entry is ¥190 plus a ¥90 shuttle (¥80 + ¥80 off-season), and it's a UNESCO World Heritage site.

🧭 Expert Tip: come mid-to-late October — red autumn leaves against the blue water are the payoff — and board the first morning shuttle before the crowds and midday glare.
